droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The six delivery fields are plain `mutableStateOf` properties on `CheckoutViewModel` (CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19), and the ViewModel has no constructor parameter for `SavedStateHandle`. ViewModel state survives only configuration changes, not process death. When the app is killed in the background, the ViewModel is discarded, and on relaunch `CheckoutScreen`'s `viewModel()` call (CheckoutScreen.kt:34) builds a fresh instance with empty strings, so every field reads as blank (CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72). The screen has no other persisted copy of the input, so the user's entries are lost, which matches the six emptied fields in the verdict.
Fix approach: Make the form state survive process death by moving it into a SavedStateHandle. Change CheckoutViewModel to take a SavedStateHandle and back each field with `savedStateHandle.getStateFlow` or `saveable` state, keyed by field name, so values are written to the saved-state bundle. Keep `isComplete` and `placeOrder` unchanged, and keep the `viewModel()` call in CheckoutScreen, which injects SavedStateHandle by default. Optionally use rememberSaveable for the field values in the composable if the ViewModel should stay simple.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:13 - CheckoutViewModel is a plain ViewModel() with no SavedStateHandle constructor parameter.; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19 - all six fields (name, email, phone, address, city, pincode) are `mutableStateOf("")` with no saved-state backing, so they are lost when the process is killed.; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - `vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel()` creates a fresh ViewModel on relaunch, so the form starts empty.; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - the six CheckoutField calls bind directly to the ViewModel's in-memory properties, with no other persisted copy of the input.; verdict - 6 of 6 filled fields changed from the entered values to '' after kill_in_background and relaunch.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test `CheckoutViewModelTest` in src/test. It creates `CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle())`, sets name, email, phone, address, city and pincode, then builds a second ViewModel from a SavedStateHandle that carries the first one's saved state (for example, `SavedStateHandle(savedState)` with the first handle's `savedStateProvider` contents). It asserts that all six fields and `isComplete` are preserved. Before the fix, the test fails to compile or the restored fields are blank. After the fix, it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.rememberScrollState
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll
import androidx.compose.material3.Button
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose.viewModel
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.OrderRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.ProductRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.priceLabel

@Composable
fun CheckoutScreen(
    productId: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val product = ProductRepository.cached(productId)
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val orders = remember { OrderRepository(context) }

    val placedId = vm.orderId
    if (placedId != null) {
        Column(modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(24.dp).testTag("order_confirmed"), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            Text("Order placed 🎉", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall)
            Text("Order $placedId is on its way to ${vm.city}.", modifier = Modifier.testTag("order_id"))
        }
        return
    }

    Column(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
            .padding(16.dp)
            .testTag("checkout_screen"),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
    ) {
        if (product != null) {
            Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
                Row(Modifier.padding(16.dp), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
                    Text("${product.emoji} ${product.name}", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
                    Text(product.priceLabel(), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.testTag("checkout_total"))
                }
            }
        }

        Text("Delivery details", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        CheckoutField("Full name", vm.name, { vm.name = it }, "field_name")
        CheckoutField("Email", vm.email, { vm.email = it }, "field_email", KeyboardType.Email)
        CheckoutField("Phone", vm.phone, { vm.phone = it }, "field_phone", KeyboardType.Phone)
        CheckoutField("Address", vm.address, { vm.address = it }, "field_address")
        CheckoutField("City", vm.city, { vm.city = it }, "field_city")
        CheckoutField("Pincode", vm.pincode, { vm.pincode = it }, "field_pincode", KeyboardType.Number)

        ScanCouponButton()

        Button(
            onClick = { vm.placeOrder(orders, productId) },
            enabled = vm.isComplete && !vm.placing,
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag("place_order"),
        ) {
            if (vm.placing) CircularProgressIndicator(Modifier.testTag("placing_order")) else Text("Place order")
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun CheckoutField(
    label: String,
    value: String,
    onChange: (String) -> Unit,
    tag: String,
    keyboard: KeyboardType = KeyboardType.Text,
) {
    OutlinedTextField(
        value = value,
        onValueChange = onChange,
        label = { Text(label) },
        singleLine = true,
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = keyboard),
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag(tag),
    )
}

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.lifecycle.SavedStateHandle
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class CheckoutViewModelTest {
    @Test
    fun formSurvivesProcessDeath() {
        val handle = SavedStateHandle()
        val first = CheckoutViewModel(handle)
        assertFalse(first.isComplete)
        first.name = "Ravi Kumar"
        first.email = "ravi@example.com"
        first.phone = "9876543210"
        first.address = "12 MG Road"
        first.city = "Bengaluru"
        first.pincode = "560001"

        val saved = handle.keys().associateWith { handle.get<Any?>(it) }
        val restored = CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle(saved))

        assertEquals("Ravi Kumar", restored.name)
        assertEquals("ravi@example.com", restored.email)
        assertEquals("9876543210", restored.phone)
        assertEquals("12 MG Road", restored.address)
        assertEquals("Bengaluru", restored.city)
        assertEquals("560001", restored.pincode)
        assertTrue(restored.isComplete)
    }
}

I moved the six checkout fields in `CheckoutViewModel` into a `SavedStateHandle`, so they now survive process death. The ViewModel takes the handle as a constructor parameter, and each field is backed by a small `savedField(key)` delegate that keeps the Compose state and writes every change to the handle. `CheckoutScreen`'s `viewModel()` call needed no change. `isComplete` and `placeOrder` are untouched.

I added `CheckoutViewModelTest` under `app/src/test`. It fills all six fields, rebuilds a second ViewModel from the first handle's saved values, and asserts the fields and `isComplete` are restored. The unit-test compile passes, but I haven't run the test or the process-death attack against the app.
